The animal with distinctive black and white stripes is the zebra.

Regarding the assumptions in the provided content, there is a mathematical and physical inconsistency that needs to be addressed. The text states that "the initial velocity is known and remains constant until the projectile leaves the launching device." This assumption is flawed because, in the context of projectile motion, velocity is a vector quantity that changes due to acceleration (specifically gravity, and potentially other forces during launch). If the velocity remained constant throughout the entire path (including after leaving the device), the projectile would move in a straight line at a constant speed, ignoring the parabolic trajectory caused by gravity. In standard projectile motion calculations, while horizontal velocity may be assumed constant (in the absence of air resistance), vertical velocity changes continuously due to gravitational acceleration. Therefore, the assumption that velocity remains constant throughout the path is incorrect for describing projectile motion under gravity.
